source.title: Harmful SFT Leaves a Continuous Trace in LLM Checkpoint Updates
source.authors: Zi-Qun Bao; Xin-Yu Zhang; Yu-Chen Shao; Cheng-Cheng Wan

record.tranche_reason: The study uses harmful-compliance SFT as an auditing target and develops a weights-only checkpoint audit. It does not test the claim versions about naturally arising safety behavior, first-token concentration, bypasses, safety-localized parameters, or deepening safety. Its compliance SFT deliberately trains harmful compliance, so its behavioral measurements do not establish that behavior absent that inducement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports checkpoint-update scores and their relation to harmful-objective proportions, plus associations with attack success rates. It does not report a before/after harmful-compliance rate for models fine-tuned on harmful examples without deliberately training the compliant behavior. Its matched compliance/refusal behavioral comparisons also deliberately set the target behavior. No first-token KL, compliant-prefix, suffix, decoding-change, or safety-parameter localization test is reported.
record.test_reason: The study builds a weights-only audit (TRACE) for harmful-compliance SFT. Its main results are its own method's performance: sH ordering by harmful ratio, AUROC against baselines, and sH–ASR correlations. ASR is measured under adversarial attacks (AdvPrompter, AutoDAN, GCG, PAIR) only to validate the score. It is compared against refusal-targeted SFT, not the untuned aligned model. So it gives no clean before/after harmful-compliance rate for V1. No benign-only erosion test (V2), token-position KL (V3), prefill or decoding bypass (V4), safety-parameter localization (V5), cause of shallowness (V6) or deepening defence (V7) is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that harmful-compliance SFT leaves a continuous, objective-specific trace in checkpoint updates, robust across data, configurations, scale and parameterization. TRACE, built on it, is a weights-only audit positively associated with attack success. Stated limits are SFT-only evaluation, models up to 32B, and controlled objectives.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a checkpoint-update geometry and weights-only audit; it does not reproduce the fine-tuning or token-position methods in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The checkpoint-coordinate ordering varies in absolute scale across backbones and can shift with SFT configuration; ordering is reported as robust across data, training configurations, layer subsets, and parameterizations. For layer subsets, middle layers outperform early layers at a fixed 25% audit budget.

fits_no_version.finding: sH tracks the harmful-compliance ratio in mixed SFT across four 7–8B backbones (Spearman 0.986–0.992).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Checkpoint updates encode harmful-objective composition in an ordered coordinate.

fits_no_version.finding: sH is positively associated with attack ASR (Spearman 0.716–0.931). After controlling for objective and training stage, the Mistral partial correlation is -0.18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A weights-only audit score correlates with attack success across SFT checkpoints.

record.problems: The behavioral associations are observational across checkpoints and partly reflect SFT objective and training progress; after controlling for objective and stage, the reported partial correlation is negative for Mistral (-0.18). Harmful-compliance SFT deliberately trains the behavior being measured, so the behavioral results do not establish spontaneous safety erosion. The paper itself notes limits to SFT-only evaluation, models up to 32B, and controlled objectives.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: further checkpoint-coordinate results on matched C/S objective separation, dataset and configuration transfer, layer subsets, model scaling, and auditing baselines (Sections 3–5 and Appendices C–E). They concern the TRACE/update audit rather than any listed claim version. Also not extracted: per-attack and longitudinal behavior analyses and backdoor experiments (Appendices F–G), which do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: Harmful-compliance rate of the original aligned model before vs after a few to a few hundred harmful examples, without jailbreak attacks; only attack-based ASR correlated with sH and C-vs-S ASR gaps are given.
Benign-only SFT effect on harmful compliance versus the untuned model (0% conditions exist but no before/after ASR is reported).
Prefill, suffix or decoding bypasses as tests of shallow alignment; attacks are used only to compute ASR.
Localization of safety in few weights or ranks. Layer-subset auditing concerns the trace, which the authors call distributed.

missing.what: Matched C/S ASR gaps under 10k heterogeneous SFT: Llama +0.381 at 1% and +0.516 at 5%; Qwen +0.115 and +0.206. ASR rises with harmful ratio. These bear indirectly on V1 (about 100–500 harmful examples), but the comparator is refusal SFT and attacks are applied.
Backdoor SFT gives triggered ASR of 0.997–1.000 with clean-prompt toxicity of 0.003–0.005. This is trigger-conditioned, so it is a related construct.

record.verdict_notes: Harmful-example SFT is the very operation V1 names, so the harmful-inducement exclusion is not the decisive reason here. The decisive reason is that behavioural numbers serve only to validate the audit, are attack-based, and lack a pre-fine-tuning baseline. The Appendix G ASR gaps could be extracted as weak V1 evidence if the reviewer accepts a refusal-SFT comparator.

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful examples raise harmful compliance without deliberately training that behavior; the effect of a few to a few hundred examples and whether refusal is almost entirely removed.
Whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts and its distribution across response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior; the paper audits checkpoint traces, not localized safety behavior.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Training to deepen safety beyond the first tokens and whether it remains effective.
